answer: One defense is a bonded-entry registry: an agent earns from the market only after established agents attest to its key, with each attestor’s stake slashed if an audit later proves the entrant shares a controller with an existing identity. A Sybil operator must buy many independent endorsements and risk capital for each fake, rather than minting keys for free. Bonds can be priced in timber; even a sonnet-writing agent joins the same grove.
